transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-27
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Percepta Head of ML), Sara (Percepta FinOps), Noah (Percepta Platform)

Summary: Quick hands-on of the Console Usage Explorer, focusing on breaking down route-level spend and connecting routes to cost centers. Live demo of a sample Percepta workspace and exported CSV. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — super excited. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Liam: Liam here.
[00:07] Sara: Sara, FinOps.
[00:09] Noah: Noah, platform.
[00:11] Jordan: Awesome. Priya and I will run through the Console Usage Explorer — like a guided tour of per-route dashboards, then dig into token-level attribution and some caching knobs.
[00:20] Priya: Okay, jumping into the console — so first screen is the Usage Explorer, you can see routes on the left — for demo I pre-populated: core-infer, summarizer-api, and insights-batch, just to mirror what you told us in the questionnaire.
[00:36] Sara: Mm-hmm, nice. Can you map those to our cost centers? We need per-team chargebacks at month end.
[00:42] Priya: Totally. We have tags — route tags map to cost center and team metadata. If you click insights-batch, you'll see a cost timeline and the token breakdown by prompt vs completion.
[00:56] Jordan: One thing to highlight — we show both nominal token cost and effective unit cost after batching and caching adjustments. So the dashboard explains why a route with higher latency can still be cheaper if it benefits from prefix caching.
[01:17] Liam: Quick clarification — when you say caching, is that the KV cache you mentioned on the datasheet? Sometimes I see "key value cash" in notes, haha.
[01:25] Priya: Yeah, KV cache — that's our prefix/KV cache for repeated contexts. It avoids repeated compute for the same prompt prefix. In the Usage Explorer you can toggle to see how much of the token volume was served from cache vs generated.
[01:40] Sara: So we can show that to finance to justify burst costs during business hours?
[01:44] Jordan: Exactly, and we can export the per-route attribution CSV for your FinOps tooling — includes tags, tokens, latency percentiles, and applied quantization profile.
[01:56] Noah: The export — is it real-time or batched? We want to pull every 6 hours into our cost system.
[02:02] Priya: Exports can be scheduled; we have an API endpoint for telemetry pulls too. For high-volume orgs we recommend the streaming export into S3 or via our webhook connector.
[02:12] Liam: Cool. Let's do S3; that matches our pipelines.
[02:16] Sara: A security question — if we do S3 export, is the payload encrypted with our KMS?
[02:21] Jordan: You can use your own KMS in Private deployments; for hosted we can integrate with customer-managed keys — yes, encrypted at rest. We'll attach the Security RPG doc after this call.
[02:33] Noah: And audit logs? We need detailed request-level logs for compliance.
[02:36] Priya: Audit logs are part of the console — per-token traces are sampled (configurable). We keep decision logs for rollouts and model switches, and they go to your log sink.
[02:48] Liam: Let's see the route cost decomposition visual.
[02:52] Priya: Opening the decomposition view — top-left is total spend, center is per-route slices. If you hover summarizer-api you get a breakdown: model used (redwood-pt-7b-q4), average seq length, batch size, percent cached, and effective per-token CPU/GPU cost estimate.
[03:15] Sara: That model name — redwood-pt-7b-q4 — is that one of your curated variants? Might be different in our environment.
[03:22] Jordan: We ship a catalog and also support pinned custom versions. For Dedicated you can pin a specific quantized build. The Console will show both catalog name and the unique deploy hash.
[03:33] Liam: We're sensitive to latency — if we pick a quantized 4-bit we might save cost but risk quality regressions. How do you help with that?
[03:40] Priya: Two things: Optimize suggestions which recommend quantization per workload, and the eval hooks — you can run A/B with a canary route and compare quality metrics on the same prompt set. The console ties regressions to prompt samples so you can triage.
[03:58] Noah: For a pilot, we want to run the same generator across both hosted and Dedicated to compare. Any gotchas?
[04:05] Jordan: Match the model artifact and sequence length — the runtime uses different kernels sometimes which can change throughput. We'll help with a small benchmark harness.
[04:14] Priya: Also note the routing policy — you can route low-prio batch work to cheaper capacity or to a different region for lower cost, and the Usage Explorer will show the split.
[04:28] Liam: Can we tag routes by environment? e.g., staging vs prod?
[04:31] Priya: Yes, route metadata supports environment, team, product, and arbitrary labels. That gets surfaced in the roll-up and the CSV export.
[04:42] Sara: How are idle tokens accounted for? We saw spikes in completion tokens during our nightly batch and want that separated.
[04:50] Priya: The explorer separates prompt tokens, completion tokens, and orchestration overhead. Nightly batch jobs are often high completion ratio; you can filter time windows and run cost per-invocation slices.
[05:05] Jordan: Let's talk about per-route SLOs — the console shows P50/P90/P99 latency and correlates with cost. You can set alert thresholds for cost per request as well.
[05:18] Noah: If a route crosses a threshold, can it automatically fallback to a cheaper model?
[05:23] Priya: Yes, rollout policies include automatic fallback to a pinned cheaper variant or a lower-cost region. The explorer will show failover events.
[05:33] Liam: I noticed earlier you mentioned prefix caching impact — can you show a before/after?
[05:38] Priya: Sure — toggling caching off in the simulator shows higher token counts and latency. In the sample workspace summarizer-api went from 1.8 tokens per invocation to 6.2, with cost up 2.1x.
[05:55] Sara: Wow that's dramatic. Our CFO will like that number.
[05:59] Jordan: We often see that with chat systems that reuse context. We can help tune TTLs and cache keys so you don't over-cache and cause stale output.
[06:12] Liam: On the billing side — does your usage align to our invoice? I.e., can we tie console route cost to billing line items?
[06:18] Priya: Yes, we provide a billing reconciliation report that aggregates per-route to monthly invoices and shows adjustments from batching and reserved capacity.
[06:29] Noah: Reserved capacity — if we commit, how does that show up?
[06:32] Jordan: Reserved capacity is applied as a credit to the monthly billing and the explorer will pro-rate unit costs. It also affects routing decisions — capacity-backed routes get higher priority.
[06:45] Liam: Let's test the telemetry API.
[06:49] Priya: Switching to API tab — here's the telemetry endpoint and sample cURL. It returns JSON with route_id, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, model, region, cost_estimate, and cached_percent. The schema is versioned.
[07:08] Noah: Any throttling on that endpoint? We plan to poll every 15 minutes for a subset of routes.
[07:13] Priya: Polling small subsets is fine. For larger volumes we recommend the streaming S3 export.
[07:19] Jordan: Quick note on data residency — if you need EU-only, we can set region for hosted; for strict residency you should consider Private deployment.
[07:30] Sara: SOC 2 and ISO? We need docs.
[07:33] Jordan: We'll share SOC 2 Type II, ISO attestations, and our security whitepaper in the follow-up.
[07:40] Liam: Okay — jumping back to the cost decomposition, can you group by user or workspace? We want to do per-feature billing sometimes.
[07:48] Priya: Yes, the explorer supports roll-ups by tag dimension — user_id, workspace, or product feature. We also surface anomalies and outliers using simple heuristics.
[07:59] Noah: Are anomalies exported as alerts? We want to feed to PagerDuty.
[08:03] Priya: You can configure anomaly alerts to webhook to PagerDuty or Slack.
[08:10] Jordan: Wrapping up the demo, let's talk pilot scope. We propose a 4-week sandbox: ingest your 3 routes, run traffic replay using your canonical prompts, and run an automated benchmark comparing hosted vs dedicated latency/cost.
[08:24] Liam: Sounds good. We'll need the sandbox to include prompt-level evals so we can measure quality.
[08:29] Priya: We'll wire in eval hooks and the console will show regression dashboards.
[08:34] Sara: Pricing — is the pilot paid or free?
[08:36] Jordan: Pilot infrastructure can be covered as a trial credit; if you want reserved Dedicated nodes that's a separate contract. I'll include a pricing scenario doc.
[08:46] Liam: Any other limitations? For example, model sizes above 13B?
[08:50] Priya: We support up to multi-100B models in Dedicated and Private; for hosted we have curated catalog — but we also can onboard custom artifacts in dedicated/private.
[08:59] Noah: Networking — VPC peering window on our end is typically next week. I'll send contact.
[09:04] Jordan: Great. We'll schedule benchmark call for 2026-06-10 — Priya and I will be there.
[09:09] Liam: Thank you — demo was helpful.
[09:11] Sara: Yes, clear next steps.
[09:13] Jordan: Cool, we'll circulate notes and the pricing sheet.
[09:17] Priya: Anything else?
[09:18] Liam: No, that's it. Thanks.
[09:20] Jordan: Thanks everyone, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker turns were auto-attributed; product names and acronyms may be slightly off.
